annotation.authors_or_issuer: Ballarin, A. (SOGEI S.p.A., for Italian Ministry of Economy and Finance)
key_provisions_or_claims: Machine learning relies on correlation over causality and abandons explainability, making errors opaque.
AI errors are inevitable, citing Gödel's incompleteness, so ethical questions arise.
Data are reductions of reality, so AI decides on simplified representations.
AI artefacts should follow non-maleficence and choose the lesser evil (trolley problem).
Proposes an 'ethical test' for AI, analogous to the Turing test, using the norms of the cognitive domain concerned.
annotation.summary_en: Slide presentation by a SOGEI author, hosted on the Italian Ministry of Economy and Finance site, on the ethical urgency of AI. It argues that data-driven machine learning sacrifices explainability and errs unavoidably. It proposes an 'ethical test' for AI artefacts, based on non-maleficence and domain norms, instead of rules-first ethics.
annotation.title_en: The Ethical Urgency of Artificial Intelligence
annotation.venue: Ministero dell'Economia e delle Finanze (MEF) website
